text: . In Cricket, New Zealand tightened their grip on the second Test after being bowled out for 356 in their first innings before reducing India to 116 for 6 at stumps on Day 2 at Hagley Oval in Christchurch today.India suffered an early setback as Matt Henry dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal for a duck in the opening over. KL Rahul scored 25 while Devdutt Padikkal scored 21. Skipper Shubman Gill contributed 17 while Pant scored 23.Earlier, New Zealand, who went into the lunch break at 330 for 8, added just 26 runs before their innings ended at 356 in 116.3 overs. Tom Blundell top-scored with 89 runs, while Tom Latham contributed 59.Akash Deep was the standout bowler for India, returning impressive figures of 5 for 99, while Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar picked up two wickets each.At the start of Day 2, India struck early after New Zealand resumed at 246/5, with Kamboj dismissing Glenn Phillips (36) at his overnight score.

. President Droupadi Murmu today said that India is making rapid progress in strengthening its armed forces and enhancing its maritime capabilities.Addressing at the Passing Out Parade of Autumn Term 2026 at the Indian Naval Academy, at Kannur, Keralam, the President underscored that the Country is strengthening its indigenous defence capabilities.She said, a growing number of warships and submarines are being designed and built in Indian shipyards, reflecting the country’s commitment to self-reliance and confidence in the capabilities of its engineers, scientists, skilled workers, and industry.The President pointed out that as officers of the Indian Navy, the cadets will be part of this journey towards a stronger and more self-reliant India. She took the salute of the cadets, and also presented medals to officer trainees who demonstrated outstanding performance during their training.A total of 427 cadets participated in today’s Passing Out Parade, including 69 women cadets and 18 cadets from foreign countries.Observing that the world is changing at an unprecedented pace, the President said that new technologies are transforming the nature of warfare and maritime security.Although all the challenges that the future would bring could not be predicted, the cadets’ training, adaptability, and commitment would prepare them to face them, she said. The President urged the cadets to continue learning and keep upgrading their knowledge and skills.The President expressed particular happiness at seeing many young women among the graduating trainees. Addressing them, the President said that their presence was a matter of pride for the entire nation.They had demonstrated that determination, courage, and competence know no boundaries. Their achievements would inspire many more young women to dream big and take up challenging responsibilities in the service of the nation.The President also extended special congratulations to the trainees from friendly foreign countries.Keralam Governor Om Prakash Mathur, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief Southern Naval Command Vice Admiral Sameer Saxena, and Commandant, Indian Naval Academy, Vice Admiral Alok Anand, were present on the occasion.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today said that Denmark is an important partner in India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.In his opening remarks at the 5th India-Denmark Joint Commission Meeting, Dr Jaishankar said that the Green Strategic Partnership has given a distinctive character to bilateral relations.He said that this collaboration brings together Denmark’s capabilities and India’s scale and development.He said both countries are cooperating in various areas, including water, renewable energy, power and green shipping.The Minister said that cooperation in health, food processing, agriculture and science and technology has also strengthened bilateral ties.The External Affairs Minister welcomed the contribution of Danish companies in India and called for expanding their business presence and activities in both countries.Dr. Jaishankar appreciated Denmark’s support in deepening the India-EU partnership, particularly for the conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.

. The Union Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship will jointly launch the second phase of Navya in Haridwar today.Union Minister Annapurna Devi and Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary, along with other dignitaries, will attend the programme.The initiative aims to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly those from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, fulfil their aspirations and contribute meaningfully to economic and social development.Akashvani correspondent reports that under the second phase of Navya, skill training will be provided to adolescent girls and young women aged between 16 and 25 years across 100 districts in 24 States and Union Territories.The initiative aims to connect them with employment, apprenticeship and self-employment opportunities, thereby making them self-reliant. Navya is an important step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment. It seeks to enable every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.Meanwhile, during the programme, Saksham Anganwadi Centres and newly constructed Anganwadi Centres under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand will also be inaugurated. Certificates will also be distributed to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana.

. The 100th edition of the nationwide ‘Fit India Sundays on Cycle’ campaign will be organised tomorrow, November 29, across the country.Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya will lead the special cycling event from Pimpri-Chinchwad in Pune. Around 50,000 cycling enthusiasts are expected to participate.Akashvani correspondent reports that with the support of MY Bharat, young people will take part in cycling events in every district across the country.In addition, 100 Indian Olympic athletes will participate in celebrations at 100 prominent locations nationwide.The theme of the landmark edition is ‘India Ready for Olympics’. Launched in December 2024, the initiative has evolved into a nationwide people’s movement promoting fitness and a healthy lifestyle.It also aims to create awareness about combating obesity, drug abuse and pollution. Inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call, ‘Fitness Ka Dose, Aadha Ghanta Roz’, the campaign encourages citizens to devote at least 30 minutes every day to physical fitness.”

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand finished the opening day of the second Test against India at 246 for five at stumps in Christchurch. Tom Blundell on 53 runs and Glenn Phillips on 36 runs were at the crease when stumps were drawn today. For India, Akash Deep claimed two wickets, while Gurnoor Brar, Washington Sundar and Anshul Kamboj picked up one wicket each. Earlier, Indian captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl. India made just one change to their playing 11, handing Gurnoor Brar his Test debut in place of Prasidh Krishna. while New Zealand remained unchanged. The first Test between the two sides had ended in a draw.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 55 paise to close at 92 rupees and 99 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.81 in intra-day trade.

. Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani stressed that India must develop its own approach to future warfare, taking lessons from global conflicts while keeping its unique security challenges in mind. He said this while delivering a lecture on the future of warfare and India’s preparedness for multi-domain operations in New Delhi yesterday.In his lecture, General Subramani highlighted that Atma Nirbharta in defence is not merely a slogan but essential for the country to sustain future military operations.The CDS also stressed that modern warfare is shifting from network-centric to decision-centric operations, with greater reliance on artificial intelligence, persistent surveillance and integrated military capabilities.General Subramani also emphasised that India must strengthen coordination among its three services and develop a joint communication network to enable faster decision-making. He also called for greater focus on space-based assets, cyber defence, electronic warfare and subterranean warfare.Drawing lessons from conflicts involving Israel, Iran, Russia and Ukraine, the CDS highlighted the importance of intelligence, long-range precision strikes, drones, artificial intelligence and cyber capabilities.He also stressed that technological superiority alone cannot win wars, as trained manpower, logistics, industrial capacity and reliable allies remain equally important.Meanwhile, citing Operation Sindoor, General Subramani praised the coordination among the armed forces, precision targeting and the effectiveness of indigenous systems such as BrahMos and Akash.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. United Nations’ food agencies have warned that hunger is expected to worsen in 16 countries over the next six months, with war-torn Sudan and Yemen among five nations facing the gravest risk. The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme’s Hunger Hotspots report places Sudan, Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria at the highest level of concern. All five have appeared on the list repeatedly since 2022.The Palestinian territories were moved down one level following the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza, though 67 percent of Gaza’s population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse. In Sudan, a risk of famine is expected to persist through January in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan. In two displacement camps in South Darfur’s Eastern Jebel Marra, acute malnutrition rates exceeded the threshold for famine.FAO Deputy Director-General Beth Bechdol said that El Nino-linked drought poses a major threat to Sudan on top of the war, compounding the conflict’s toll on food production. In Yemen, the report said, hunger is likely to worsen as fighting that resumed in July spreads across multiple fronts. The country has been at war since 2014, when the Iran-backed Houthi rebels seized the capital, Sanaa, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene the following year.

. Global crude oil prices rose moderately today amid sporadic hostilities in West Asia, raising concerns over potential disruptions to oil supplies. Brent crude was trading 0.2 per cent up at 96 US dollars and 75 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 85 US dollars and 35 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.Global investors will closely monitor the 42nd OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting, scheduled to take place in Austria this Sunday, as member countries deliberate on oil production policy for the coming calendar year.

. Union Minister of Finance  Nirmala Sitharaman  has   concluded the  extensive pre-budget consultation meetings for the preparation of the Union Budget 2027-28. Ms Sitharaman today chaired the 13th and final Pre-Budget Consultation with youth for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The first consultation meeting was held on 16th of this month. Ministry of Finance has said that more than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the consultations.These include industry associations, domain experts,  youth representatives and practitioners from Agriculture and Rural Development; Manufacturing, MSMEs and Startups; Capital Markets and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance, Information Technology, Infrastructure, Energy and Sustainability and Employment and Labour.The consultation meeting with youth representatives was a novel initiative this year. The Ministry said that the the consultations generated a wide range of forward-looking recommendations aimed at strengthening India’s human capital, innovation ecosystem, manufacturing competitiveness, agricultural productivity, housing security, and educational outcomes. Stakeholders emphasized the need for reforms that can further accelerate economic growth while ensuring broad-based and inclusive development.Collectively, the recommendations focused on promoting innovation-led growth, expanding employment opportunities, strengthening social and economic infrastructure, and building a more resilient and future-ready economy.The pre-budget consultations form an important part of the Government’s participatory and consultative approach to budget-making, enabling diverse stakeholders to contribute to shaping India’s development priorities and growth agenda.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has invoked Lord Murugan hours after the Supreme Court ordered the lighting of the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon pillar on Thiruparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district.In a social media post, Mr Modi wrote in Tamil, Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara, which translates to Victory to Lord Murugan. Yesterday, the Supreme Court issued a contempt notice to the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai collector and others over the violation of its Karthigai Deepam order.The Apex Court suspended the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and ordered lighting of lamp at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon today using the flame lit at Uchaipillaiyar mandapam.Asking the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary to appear personally, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi directed him to file an affidavit detailing emails, calls, and messages exchanged between officials.The bench said that the wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand.

. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor today reaffirmed America’s commitment to freedom of navigation and cooperation on maritime security, energy, infrastructure, and critical minerals. In a social media post, Mr. Gor said, open sea lanes are essential to global trade and prosperity. He attended the 25th Council of Ministers (COM) Meeting of Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) in New Delhi today.The meeting is being held under India’s IORA 2025-2027 chairship with the theme of Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region. During the meeting, Mauritius and Sri Lanka has lauded India’s IORA chairmanship.Mauritius Foreign Minister Dhananjay Ramful praised India for successfully hosting the 25th Council of Ministers (COM) meeting of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) and commended its chairmanship of the regional grouping over the past year. In his remarks at the meeting, Ramful highlighted Mauritius’ commitment to working closely with India and other member states in its new role as the association’s Vice-Chair. Mr. Ramful highlighted IORA’s potential to serve as a key platform for fostering regional cooperation, promoting sustainable and inclusive economic growth, and addressing common challenges among its member states.Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath highlighted the continued relevance of that vision under country’s current chairmanship of IORA, noting that the theme adopted by India reflected the challenges facing the region. Herath said, Sri Lanka looks forward to working closely with both India and Mauritius in the troika.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, in Goa is highlighting the growing contribution of women to cinema. 52 women filmmakers are participating in this year’s festival.Indian women filmmakers are leading from the front, bringing diverse narratives and fresh perspectives.Leena Yadav’s Ladakhi film Becoming explores themes of spirituality and destiny. While, Muskan Asthana’s Sev Micchar, Anupama Sharadhi’s Pili Channe and Antara G G Choudhury’s Surjyamukhi further add to the diversity of Indian storytelling.The festival is also showcasing compelling voices from across the world. Kyrgyz filmmaker Narghiza Dotieva’s Skylark explores the impact of border disputes on a teenager’s life. Romanian-Roma filmmaker Alina Șerban’s film I Matter was the mid-fest film. In a media interaction Sherban, who has roots in India, became emotional.From challenging stereotypes and examining social realities to exploring identity, culture and women’s experiences, these filmmakers are bringing fresh perspectives to the screen.

. Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam in Varanasi today. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi along with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, were present on the occasion. The event will continue until December 12.The theme of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 is “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”, meaning “Let us Learn the Thirukkural”. It is the celebrated work of the great Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar.The focus is on fostering awareness and understanding of the timeless wisdom of the Thirukkural, particularly among students and youth, while encouraging appreciation of India’s rich literary traditions and enduring cultural heritage.

. Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have moved a step closer to winning their third consecutive women’s doubles title at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 Badminton Tournament. Meanwhile, Tanvi Sharma and Unnati Hooda have entered the women’s singles semi-finals.Top seeds Treesa and Gayatri advanced to the semi-finals after receiving a walkover from seventh-seeded French pair Margot Lambert and Camille Pognante in the quarter-finals.In women’s singles, second seed Tanvi Sharma defeated Indonesia’s Ni Kadek Dhinda Amartya Pratiwi in a hard-fought three-game encounter, 21-19, 18-21, 21-14. Third seed Unnati Hooda also secured a hard-fought victory over compatriot Anmol Kharb, winning 21-19, 15-21, 21-18.With Tanvi and Unnati set to face each other in the semi-finals, an all-Indian finalist in women’s singles is now assured. In the other semi-final, top seed Riko Gunji of Japan will take on fourth seed Supanida Katethong of Thailand.Gunji defeated India’s Tasnim Mir 21-11, 21-11 in the quarter-finals, ending her campaign. Earlier, Tasnim had caused an upset by defeating sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour of Scotland in the pre-quarter-finals.In mixed doubles, India’s Satwik Reddy Kanapuram and Resika Uthayasooryan defeated compatriots Viraj Kuvale and Rituparna Panda 21-8, 21-14 to enter the semi-finals. They will face Malaysia’s pair of V. Y. Hern and Vani Gobi in the last four.

. The Indian women’s hockey team continued its impressive winning run at the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy, securing a convincing 4-0 victory over Japan in Bhopal ahead of the semi-finals.Deepika starred with two goals, while Lalremsiami and Neha added one goal each to seal India’s emphatic win. Navneet Kaur was named Player of the Match and dedicated the award to the entire team. India’s impressive campaign has also propelled the team to fourth place in the world rankings, providing an additional boost ahead of the knockout stage.In the other matches, Malaysia defeated Thailand 4-0, while China secured a narrow 1-0 win over Korea.India will now face Malaysia in the semi-final on tomorrow, as the hosts aim to continue their winning run and move closer to the title. The tournament will conclude on November 28, with the bronze-medal match at 4:30 PM, followed by the final at 7 PM.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. The Union Cabinet has approved the Delimitation Amendment Bill and the bill related to Women’s reservation. In a social media post, Minister for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal said that the enactment of the bills will pave the way for a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats across all states, as well as a 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The Minister said that the proposed delimitation framework marks a significant step towards reshaping India’s parliamentary landscape. He said that this initiative will open new opportunities for leadership and representation for millions of women across the country.He added that the growing participation of women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies will give a new voice to their aspirations and a new direction to the decision-making process.Mr Meghwal said that a historic step has been taken under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with the resolve to further strengthen the participation of women in the country’s policy-making and decision-making processes.The Minister said that the proposed delimitation framework marks a significant step towards reshaping India’s parliamentary landscape. He said that the Lok Sabha’s strength is set to rise from the existing 543 seats to 816 in the proposed bill. He emphasised that every state and Union Territory stands to witness an expansion in its parliamentary representation.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has hailed the approval of the Delimitation Amendment Bill by the Union Cabinet, reaffirming the government’s unwavering commitment to fulfilling the promise made to the Nari Shakti of the country.Sharing a video message in a social media post, Mr Modi said that the government had made a promise to the women of the country, and it remains firmly committed to fulfilling it.Mr Modi said, our resolve to empower Nari Shakti remains unshaken. The Prime Minister added that the fight to give women representation has been going on for decades and I am one of those trying to make it happen.Home Minister Amit Shah lauded the approval of the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill and the bill related to Women’s Reservation by the Union Cabinet.In a social media post, he said that ensuring strong representation for women in elected bodies has been a firm commitment of the Modi government. Mr Shah said that the decades-long wait of the nation’s women is finally coming to an end under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.He said that the 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, envisioned through the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, is now set to become a reality. Mr Shah expressed hope that all political parties would extend their support to this historic initiative, which empowers women to become strong partners in governance.

. Kuwait today summoned Iran’s Ambassador Mohammad Totonji and handed him a formal note of protest over continued Iranian attacks on the country.The move follows a drone attack on Thursday targeting a vital site in Kuwait, which killed two Italian nationals and injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national. The attack also caused extensive material damage. Iran, however, had denied their involvement in the attack.Kuwait’s Deputy Foreign Minister Hamad Sulaiman Al-Mishaan called the attacks as a violation of Kuwait’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a breach of international law and the UN Charter. He also held Iran fully responsible for the attacks and their consequences.

. Global fashion retailers, including Zara, H&M and Marks & Spencer, have shifted around $254 million worth of garment orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs, primarily India, amid labour unrest, rising production costs and delivery disruptions.According to a Reuters report, three garment factory owners said the order diversions took place between November 1 and 18, with India emerging as the biggest beneficiary. Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia are also attracting orders as international buyers seek more reliable supply chains.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) estimates that labour protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses. The garment sector accounts for over 80 per cent of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40 per cent of its manufacturing jobs.Industry representatives said rising wages, energy shortages, higher raw-material costs and political uncertainty have weakened Bangladesh’s competitive advantage. Bangladesh’s production and delivery cycle reportedly takes around 120 days, compared with 60 to 90 days in competing countries.The development follows Bangladesh’s approval of a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, which triggered fresh protests.Industry leaders have warned that temporary order shifts could become long-term sourcing decisions unless political stability and uninterrupted production are restored.

. In hockey, Defending champions India have stormed into the final of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy, defeating Malaysia 6-2 this evening.In the second semi-final, India dominated the match, scoring five of their six goals through penalty corners at the International Sports Complex in Bhopal .Mumtaz Khan opened the scoring in the 10th minute, before Navneet Kaur doubled India’s lead with a field goal in the 18th minute. Deepika scored twice, while Sunelita Toppo and Ishika added one goal each. For Malaysia Nur Azhar and Nuramirah Zulkifli netted on goal each.Earlier in the first semifinal, China beat Japan 1-0 . The title clash between India and China will be played tomorrow at 7 PM.

. Ambassador of the European Union to India Jean-Eric Paquet today said that the landmark India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will be formally signed on 16th of next month during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Brussels.Talking to a News Agency, Mr. Paquet said that negotiations on the pact are complete and the agreement is ready for signature. He said, after signing of the agreement, the deal will undergo scrutiny and approval by the European Parliament.Highlighting the commercial impact of the pact, Mr. Paquet said bilateral trade which stood at 118 billion Euro in goods in 2025 is poised for major expansion once duties are dismantled. He said, the FTA will certainly allow a very strong acceleration of the growth of that trade. He confirmed that duties will fall sharply as soon as the pact takes effect, benefiting both Indian exporters and European consumers across key sectors such as textiles, food, and high-value goods.

. Country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 4.4 billion US dollars to 700.9 billion US dollars during the week ended on 20th of this month. According to the Reserve Bank of India’s data, Gold reserves dropped over 4 billion US dollars to 94.5 billion US dollars during the week.Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, slipped by 266 million US dollars to 583.2 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 67 million US dollars to 18.45 billion US dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund lost 15 million US dollars to 4.74 billion US dollars.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India is marking its seventh day in Goa with tributes to cinematic legends, masterclasses and special film screenings. The festival today honoured veteran actor Nana Patekar through a special screening of his acclaimed film Diksha, as part of the Homage section.Day Seven of the 57th International Film Festival of India opens on an exciting note as Rishab Shetty’s much-awaited Kannada film Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1 is being screened this morning in the International Competition section.Directed by and starring Rishab Shetty, the 169-minute film follows Berme, a young forest dweller, who enters the neighbouring kingdom of Bangra and witnesses the oppression of forest communities by its rulers. When Prince Kulashekara launches an attack on the tribes, Berme joins their struggle for justice and dharma.Blending spectacular visuals, indigenous traditions, and action, the film brings a distinctive cultural narrative from India’s regional cinema to an international platform.With Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1 competing alongside films from across the world, IFFI once again highlights how deeply rooted local stories can find a universal audience through the language of cinema.Acclaimed casting director and filmmaker Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged’ at Kala Academy, Panaji, on the seventh day today as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). During the 90-minute session, Chhabra spoke about how actors are chosen for films, the importance of auditions and the process of finding the right person for each role. Sharing his experiences from films such as Rockstar, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Dangal, Jawan and Dhurandhar, he spoke about finding new talent from different parts of the country and understanding what a director wants from a character.Blending creativity, technology and innovation, the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) is drawing attention at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) with a showcase of emerging opportunities in the creative technology sector. Established by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, IICT is a national-level institute dedicated to Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics and Extended Reality (AVGC-XR).The stall offers visitors a glimpse into the growing possibilities in these fields, highlighting career opportunities, academic programmes and skill development initiatives. It also showcases the institute’s efforts in startup incubation, policy development and research aimed at strengthening India’s creative technology ecosystem.Adding an interactive touch to the showcase, the stall features the ‘Doodle Dash: The Movie Poster Challenge’, a creative competition inviting participants to bring movie posters to life through their artistic skills. The challenge offers prizes worth over one lakh rupees, along with scholarships of up to 30 per cent on IICT’s two-year programmes.Through its academic and innovation-driven initiatives, IICT aims to nurture skilled talent, encourage creative entrepreneurship and support the growth of India’s AVGC-XR industry.

. In Chess, reigning world champion D Gukesh played out a quick 20-move draw with Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov in the second game of the FIDE World Championship in Geneva yesterday.Playing with white, Gukesh opted for the London System but failed to gain an advantage as Sindarov comfortably equalised. The Indian agreed to a draw by threefold repetition, with all 30 remaining pieces still on the board.Both players are now level at one point each after two games of the 14-game championship match.The third game will be played tomorrow, with Sindarov having the white pieces.

. Acclaimed casting director and filmmaker Mukesh Chhabra conducted a masterclass titled ‘The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged’ at Kala Academy, Panaji, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).During the 90-minute session, Chhabra spoke about how actors are chosen for films, the importance of auditions and the process of finding the right person for each role. Sharing his experiences from films such as Rockstar, Bajrangi Bhaijaan, Dangal, Jawan and Dhurandhar, he spoke about finding new talent from different parts of the country and understanding what a director wants from a character.Addressing aspiring actors, Chhabra said, “Rejection is part of life. I don’t reject an actor, I only reject a character. My job is to fit with the director’s vision.” He encouraged young actors to keep working hard, learn from every opportunity and not give up after rejection. “Auditions can change your life,” he said, adding that actors should be open to guidance and direction.Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker praised Chhabra, calling people like him an asset to the film industry. Recalling the making of Lagaan, Gowariker said finding the right actors was a real struggle, as professional casting directors were not part of the process in the way they are today. He spoke about how casting directors help filmmakers find the right actors for their stories.Chhabra, who also directed Dil Bechara, recalled how Gangs of Wasseypur changed his life.The masterclass was part of IFFI’s knowledge-sharing sessions under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’.

India presented its “vision and proposed roadmap” for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee’s Future Host Commission yesterday. The 30-minute presentation was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission.The presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad’s preparedness, including sports infrastructure and the support extended by the city, state, and central authorities to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). It also covered India’s experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games.Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Türkiye are the other countries that are bidding for the 2036 Games. After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an “anonymous survey” to get a sense of the general public’s view on India’s bid. The survey is expected to be done in the third week of December and will have a bearing on the evaluation of India’s bid in March next year, following which the phase of Strategic Dialogue will start. During this phase, the interested countries will be expected to provide an initial response to the Future Host Questionnaire and core financial guarantees.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan today paid tributes to social activist and reformer Mahatma Jyotirao Phule on his death anniversary. In a social media post, the Vice President said that Mahatma Jyotirao Phule dedicated his life to social equality, justice and education.He described Mahatma Phule as a pioneer of women’s education and a tireless champion of the rights of the marginalised sections of society. Mr Radhakrishnan said that Mahatma Jyotirao Phule’s commitment to building an inclusive and equitable society continues to inspire generations. He added that Phule’s ideals remain a guiding light in the country’s pursuit of a just and progressive Bharat.Union Home Minister Amit Shah has paid tributes to Mahatma Jyotiba Phule on his death anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Shah described Jyotiba Phule as a pioneer of social revolution. He said that Mr Phule firmly believed that education was the most powerful means of bringing change and progress in society.The Home Minister said that by opening schools for girls, Mahatma Phule laid a strong foundation for women’s education. He added that through the establishment of Satyashodhak Samaj, Mahatma Phule showed the path of harmony and equality.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading 0.8 per cent up at 95 US dollars and 38 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.2 per cent higher at 84 US dollars and 65 cent per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has raised concerns over disruptions to agricultural exports through the Black Sea region amid the ongoing war with Russia. He warned that the impact extends far beyond the region and threatens food supplies to hundreds of millions of people across the world. He said, Russia’s war had made agricultural exports from the Black Sea region significantly more difficult, affecting countries dependent on Ukrainian food products, including grain, flour and sunflower oil.Highlighting Ukraine’s contribution to global food supplies, the Ukrainian President said the country’s farmers and food producers supply dozens of agricultural products to international markets, warning that disruptions could lead to shortages and rising prices.

A new hostel building for Shree Dibya Deep Secondary School in Mustang district of Nepal was inaugurated today under the Government of India’s High Impact Community Development Project programme.The hostel, constructed with financial assistance from the Government of India, was jointly inaugurated by Dr. Rakesh Pandey, Deputy Chief of Mission at the Embassy of India in Kathmandu, and Tashi Nharbu Gurung, Chairman of Lomanthang Rural Municipality in Gandaki Province.The project has been implemented through Lomanthang Rural Municipality and is expected to improve accommodation facilities for students and strengthen the educational infrastructure in the region.India has undertaken 605 High Impact Community Development Projects across all seven provinces of Nepal. Of these, 64 projects are in Gandaki Province, including 18 in Mustang district.India has also gifted 126 ambulances and 52 school buses to institutions in the health and education sectors of Gandaki Province, including 11 ambulances and six school buses in Mustang.The project reflects the continued development partnership between India and Nepal, with a focus on supporting local communities and strengthening infrastructure in priority sectors.

. In Cricket, Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets to reach the final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha last night. Chasing a target of 318 runs, Sri Lanka A scored 318 runs with the loss of 2 wickets in 41.3 overs against India A in the first semi-final. Opting to bat first, India A scored 317 runs, losing 8 wickets in the stipulated 50 overs. For India A, Abhishek Sharma scored the highest score, 78 runs off 63 balls. Since Jayawardena was declared player of the match. Sri Lanka: A opener, Sineth, scored 105 off 70 balls.Sri Lanka A will play the final on Sunday. The opponent will be decided today, when Pakistan A faces Bangladesh A in the 2nd Semi-Final at 3:30 PM IST in Doha.

. Amid a liquidity crunch in the banking system, the Reserve Bank has reduced the minimum daily maintenance of cash reserve ratio – CRR from 99 percent to 90 percent. In a notification issued today, RBI said the decision has been taken on the basis of an assessment of current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions. It added that the decision will be effective from the fortnight beginning 1st December 2026.The move comes days after the banking system liquidity turned to deficit for the first time in five months on the back of Goods and Services Tax outflows and the RBI’s foreign exchange market interventions.

Bangladesh’s Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has filed a case naming 5,008 people in connection with an attack on its personnel and incidents of arson in Tungipara upazila of Gopalganj district, according to local media reports.The case relates to violence on November 17 at Nilfa Bazar in Tungipara, where a BGB patrol reportedly came under attack. Eight people have been named, while 5,000 others remain unidentified accused. Those named include Gopalganj Chhatra League General Secretary Ataur Rahman Pial and several current and former Tungipara upazila Chhatra League leaders.Media reports said the incident also involved arson and damage to property, with estimated losses amounting to around 6.51 crore taka.The incidents have drawn attention to the security situation in Gopalganj, where attacks on law enforcement personnel and damage to public and private property have raised concerns.Authorities are investigating the incidents and identifying those allegedly involved. Further details regarding arrests and the progress of the investigation are awaited.

IndiGo has resumed select flight operations to and from Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah and Madinah, while extending the suspension of services to Riyadh and Dammam until December 7, amid prevailing regional tensions.In a travel advisory posted on social media, the airline said the decision was taken after assessing the prevailing situation and operational considerations. It said affected passengers were being informed through their registered contact details and advised travellers to check flight status on its website or mobile app before leaving for the airport.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh also shared the advisory, confirming the continued suspension of flights to Riyadh and Dammam.The development comes after a Houthi attack on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s Jazan region on Thursday killed one person. The attack drew strong condemnation from the Arab League, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and Qatar.

Jeay Sindh Freedom Movement (JSFM) Chairman Sohail Abro has accused Pakistan’s security agencies of systematically targeting Sindhi nationalist activists through enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings and intimidation. He alleged that peaceful voices opposing the exploitation of Sindh’s natural resources are being suppressed by the Pakistani administration.In an interview to a News Agency, Abro alleged that personnel from Pakistan’s Counter-Terrorism Department and police attempted to abduct JSFM leader Saeed Tunio from his shop, while his two younger brothers, Saleem and Naeem, were taken away and remain missing. According to Abro, Tunio resisted the attempt, and residents intervened, preventing his detention. However, his brothers were allegedly taken away by the authorities. He stated that police subsequently registered a case against Tunio’s father, accusing him and others of attacking officers.Abro alleged that more than 350 Sindhi nationalist activists have been subjected to enforced disappearances over the years. He cited several cases, including that of Sajan Malookani, an 18-year-old law student whose mutilated body was reportedly handed over to his family in 2025 after he was allegedly picked up from college. Accusing Pakistan of exploiting Sindh’s oil, gas, coal and other mineral resources, Abro stated that the province’s population continues to face electricity and gas shortages despite its substantial natural wealth. He alleged that nearly 76.7 per cent of the revenue generated from Sindh is taken away in the name of the federal government.

The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, which brought together films and filmmakers from across the world, is set to conclude today, marking the end of another vibrant celebration of the art of cinema.On the final day, the festival continues with a selection of films, including Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Health Centre and Azad Bharath. Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen’s We Are All Strangers will be screened as the closing film.The festival will culminate with the closing ceremony this evening at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium. More from our correspondent:Nine days of cinematic celebration, inspiring stories and unforgettable moments are now drawing to a close in Goa. Across the festival venues, screenings continue to bring audiences a wide range of stories, perspectives and filmmaking traditions.The closing film, We Are All Strangers, directed by Anthony Chen, will bring the festival’s cinematic showcase to a fitting conclusion. Talking to Akashvani News today, the film’s lead actors, Koh Jia Ler and Regene Lim, expressed their delight at being part of IFFI’s closing film. They said they hope the film would help strengthen the cultural and cinematic connection between India and Singapore.This year’s edition, held under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, also placed a special emphasis on nurturing emerging talent and strengthening opportunities within the film industry. Initiatives such as Page Se Pitch Tak provided aspiring filmmakers with a platform to present their ideas and compete for recognition.Creative Minds of Tomorrow brought together young filmmaking talents for an intensive 48-hour challenge, encouraging collaboration and creativity.Additionally, the WAVES Film Bazaar further strengthened industry engagement, facilitating networking, business opportunities and international collaborations. As the curtains come down on the 57th edition, IFFI leaves behind a celebration of cinema that transcends languages, cultures and geographical boundaries.Meanwhile, Director of the Hindi film “Hanuman Ansh”, Dr. Vishal Chaturvedi, interacted with the media at a press conference during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. The film is featured in the Indian Panorama section of the festival.Speaking about the film, Dr Chaturvedi described it as a personal and spiritual journey inspired by the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba.He said he wanted to keep the film simple and minimalist, without unnecessary elements, allowing the story and emotions to speak for themselves. This approach is reflected in the film’s production design, costumes, colours and music.He said his long-standing connection with music played an important role in shaping the film. His three-year musical journey after arriving in Mumbai helped him understand music better and work closely with talented musicians. He added that music was used according to the emotional needs of each scene, with minimal instruments wherever required.Sharing his experience as a first-time director, he spoke about the financial challenges he faced while making the film. He said his determination to tell the story helped him overcome these difficulties and bring the film to the screen.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has permitted foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically (non-cash) settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts. In a circular issued today, SEBI said the move is aimed at deepening institutional participation and enhancing liquidity in the commodity derivatives segment. Currently, FPIs are permitted to participate in the commodity derivatives segment of recognised stock exchanges only through cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts. The new framework, will however allow FPIs to trade in non-cash settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, excluding options in goods, subject to specified safeguards.Under the new framework, FPIs can hold positions in physically settled contracts only until the commencement of the tender or staggered delivery period and will have to square off or roll over their open positions before the start of the delivery period. SEBI has further prescribed a safeguard mechanism for cases where FPIs fail to voluntarily close or roll over their positions. The new framework will come into effect from 1st June, 2027.

Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

A series of crude bomb explosions were reported at several locations in Dhaka on Friday evening and late at night, while three buses were set on fire in Savar and Ashulia in the early hours of Saturday, raising security concerns in and around the Bangladesh capital. According to Local Media reports.Police said explosions occurred in the Kalabagan, Wari, Kafrul and Dhanmondi areas, with additional blasts reported in Gabtoli and Mohakhali.Two crude bombs were detonated in front of Eastern Plaza in Hatirpool, and police detained a suspect, identified as Mizan, in connection with the incident. No casualties were reported.Meanwhile, three buses were set on fire in separate incidents in Savar and Ashulia between 1:30 am and 4:30 am on Saturday.Two buses were torched in Bolibhadra and Narsinghapur areas of Ashulia, while another was set ablaze near Bank Town along the Dhaka-Aricha highway in Savar.Fire service personnel brought the fires under control. Police said investigations were underway to identify those responsible and take legal action.

. Reigning world champion D. Gukesh held challenger Javokhir Sindarov to a draw with the black pieces in Game 3 of the 2026 FIDE World Chess Championship in Geneva yesterday. The players are now tied at 1.5 points apiece heading into today’s rest day.Gukesh looked well prepared for the opening and handled Sindarov’s attempts to gain an advantage with confidence. Even when computer evaluations suggested that white had the upper hand, the Indian appeared to know exactly where to find the right moves and how to keep his position intact. The draw also leaves him with the white pieces in the next game.With 11 games still remaining in the 14-game match, it appears Gukesh has a few surprises up his sleeve in terms of preparation, while Sindarov has some questions to answer about his own match preparation. As per the rules, the first player to reach 7.5 points will win the title. In case of a 7-7 tie after 14 games, shorter-format games will be played to determine the winner.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices snapped their two-day winning streak today. The Sensex shed 989 points or 1.17 per cent to close at 83 thousand 339. The Nifty fell 277 points or 1.07 per cent to settle at 25 thousand 607.However, in the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index edged up 0.1 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index rose almost 0.6 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 24 out of 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, HCL Tech plummeted 2.8 per cent, Infosys as well as Tata Consultancy Services lost 2.5 per cent, Bajaj Finserv dropped 2.2 per cent. In contrast, Bharat Electronics limited jumped 1.6 per cent, Titan rose almost one per cent, and Indigo gained half a per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 20 out of 28 sectors edged lower. Among the top laggards, IT fell 1.5 per cent, Focused IT as well as Realty lost nearly 1.4 per cent, and Auto declined 1.3 per cent. In contrast, Capital Goods climbed 1.6 per cent, Metal advanced one per cent, and Industrials gained 0.9 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 396 companies advanced, 1 thousand 969 declined and 252 remained unchanged.

. Today is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The day is observed on November 25 every year to raise awareness about violence against women and girls and call for an end to abuse and discrimination. This year, the United Nations marks the day under the theme, UNITE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity.The theme highlights the need for stronger justice systems, safe reporting mechanisms, better support services for survivors and accountability for perpetrators. It also recognizes that violence against women takes place in homes, workplaces, public spaces and online.According to the UN, one in three women worldwide experiences physical or sexual violence during her lifetime. However, many survivors still struggle to access justice, protection and support due to fear, social stigma, discrimination and weak institutional responses.

South Korea’s Kospi surged 4.3 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite gained 3.7 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng as well as Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 2.1 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times added nearly 0.7 per cent, and Taiwan’s Taiex added 0.4 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose 0.9 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 gained 0.8 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Defending champions India will take on China in a high-stakes final of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 at the International Sports Complex in Bhopal today. The title clash is scheduled to begin at 7 PM Indian Standard Time.India stormed into the final after registering a convincing 6-2 victory over Malaysia in the second semi-final yesterday evening. The Indian team produced a dominant performance, with five of their six goals coming from penalty corners.Mumtaz Khan opened the scoring in the 10th minute, while Navneet Kaur extended India’s lead with a field goal in the 18th minute. Deepika struck twice, while Sunelita Toppo and Ishika also found the net to complete India’s emphatic victory.Earlier, China secured their place in the final with a narrow 1-0 win over Japan in the first semi-final.
